question: Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state (HHS) is characterised by significant ketonaemia and metabolic acidosis, similar to diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. HHS differs fundamentally from DKA: in HHS there is enough residual insulin to suppress lipolysis, so ketones are absent or minimal and there is no significant acidosis. The hallmark of HHS is extreme hyperosmolality.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. HHS has markedly elevated glucose (often >600 mg/dL) and hyperosmolality but minimal or absent ketonaemia, because residual insulin suppresses lipolysis. This distinguishes it from DKA.
